```{r}
results_date    = "20260813"
# scDblFinder expected doublet rate and its tolerance, from the PIPseq T20
# multiplet specification (see Doublet removal)
dbr             = 0.08
dbr_sd          = 0.02
# neighbors per cell in the SNN graph that Louvain clusters
snn_k           = 30
# mean log fold change a marker must reach to enter the working list
lfc_thresh      = 1
genome_dir      = "/mnt/research/bioinformaticsCore/shared/Genomes/Petromyzon_marinus"
marker_file     = "canonical_markers_S1_only_2026-08-14.csv"
ieg_marker_file = "immediate_early_markers_2026-10-06.csv"
```

```{r}
# The doublet-filtered per-sample objects and the merge are cached in the shared
# _no_doublets directory and reused from there when they already exist.
object_dir  = paste0(params$project_dir, "/results/", results_date,
                     "_no_doublets")
results_dir = paste0(params$project_dir, "/results/", results_date,
                     "_atlas")
Robject_out_dir = paste0(results_dir, "/Robjects")
data_dir    = paste0(params$project_dir, "/data")

for (d in c(object_dir, results_dir, Robject_out_dir))
  if (!dir.exists(d)) dir.create(d, recursive = TRUE)

all_sce_file   = paste0(object_dir, "/all.sce.Rds")
mnn_file       = paste0(object_dir, "/mnn.sce.Rds")
merged_file    = paste0(object_dir, "/merged.sce.Rds")
combined_file  = paste0(object_dir, "/combined.sce.Rds")
dbl_stats_file = paste0(object_dir, "/doublet_removal_stats.csv")
rate_stamp     = paste0(object_dir, "/doublet_rate_used.txt")
k_stamp        = paste0(object_dir, "/clustering_k_used.txt")

build_all_sce  = !file.exists(all_sce_file)
build_mnn      = !file.exists(mnn_file)
build_combined = !file.exists(combined_file)

# the cache directory is shared, so objects built at another doublet rate must
# not be silently reused
if (build_all_sce) {
  writeLines(paste0("dbr=", dbr, " dbr_sd=", dbr_sd), rate_stamp)
} else if (file.exists(rate_stamp)) {
  prev = readLines(rate_stamp)[1]
  now  = paste0("dbr=", dbr, " dbr_sd=", dbr_sd)
  if (!identical(prev, now))
    stop("Objects in ", object_dir, " were built at ", prev,
         " rather than ", now, ". Delete the cached objects and reknit.")
}

# and the same for k, since the clustering is cached alongside the merge
if (!file.exists(merged_file)) {
  build_merged = TRUE
} else if (file.exists(k_stamp)) {
  prev_k = as.integer(readLines(k_stamp)[1])
  build_merged = !identical(prev_k, as.integer(snn_k))
  if (build_merged)
    message("Cached clustering used k = ", prev_k, "; reclustering at k = ",
            snn_k, ".")
} else {
  # an object written before this document existed, so the k it used is not
  # recorded. Reclustered rather than assumed, which is cheap next to the merge.
  warning("No k stamp in ", object_dir,
          "; the cached clustering's k is unknown. Reclustering at k = ",
          snn_k, ".")
  build_merged = TRUE
}
```

# Doublet removal

Doublets are removed per sample, before any normalization, HVG selection or PCA,
and before the samples are merged.

`scDblFinder` documents `dbr` as *"The expected doublet rate. By default this is
assumed to be 1% per thousand cells captured (so 4% among 4000 thousand cells),
which is appropriate for 10x datasets."* At roughly 16,700 cells per library
that default expects about 16.7% doublets.

These libraries are PIPseq T20 3' v4.0. Cell concentration was adjusted to
4 x 10^6 cells/ml and 10 ul loaded, which is 40,000 cells, the standard
protocol. The kit user guide states that this gives recovery above 20,000 cells
and a multiplet rate below 8%.

```{r, eval=build_all_sce}
sample_dirs  = list.dirs(data_dir, full.names = TRUE, recursive = FALSE)
sample_dirs  = sample_dirs[grep("smith_annotation", sample_dirs, invert = TRUE)]
sample_names = basename(sample_dirs)

cds_list = list()
for (i in seq_along(sample_dirs)) {
  cds_list[[i]] = readRDS(paste0(sample_dirs[i], "/", sample_names[i],
                                 "_cds_mito_filter.Rds"))
}
names(cds_list) = sample_names

all.sce = list()
for (cds in names(cds_list)) {
  raw_counts     = counts(cds_list[[cds]])
  all.sce[[cds]] = SingleCellExperiment(list(counts = raw_counts),
                                        colData = cds_list[[cds]]@colData)
  all.sce[[cds]]@colData$sample = cds
}
```

```{r, eval=build_all_sce}
set.seed(100)
all.sce.dbl = lapply(all.sce, function(x)
  scDblFinder(x, dbr = dbr, dbr.sd = dbr_sd))

n_before = sapply(all.sce, ncol)
n_dbl    = sapply(all.sce.dbl, function(x) sum(x$scDblFinder.class == "doublet"))

for (cds in names(all.sce)) {
  keep = colData(all.sce.dbl[[cds]])$scDblFinder.class == "singlet"
  all.sce[[cds]] = all.sce[[cds]][, keep]
}

n_after = sapply(all.sce, ncol)
                                                                                                     
write.csv(data.frame(sample = names(n_before), n_before = n_before,
                     n_doublet = n_dbl, n_after = n_after,
                     pct_doublet = round(100 * n_dbl / n_before, 2),
                     row.names = NULL),
          file = dbl_stats_file, row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r, eval=build_all_sce}
all.sce  <- lapply(all.sce, logNormCounts)
all.dec  <- lapply(all.sce, modelGeneVar)
all.hvgs <- lapply(all.dec, getTopHVGs, prop = 0.1)
all.sce  <- mapply(FUN = runPCA, x = all.sce, subset_row = all.hvgs)
saveRDS(all.sce, file = all_sce_file)
```

# Merge

Samples are merged with `fastMNN` and embedded with UMAP and t-SNE. 

```{r}
if (build_mnn) {
  if (file.exists(merged_file)) {
    # A clustered object already exists from an earlier run. fastMNN's corrected
    # space does not depend on k, so it is reused rather than recomputed.
    mnn.sce <- readRDS(merged_file)
  } else {
    # recomputed here rather than carried from above, which does not run when
    # all.sce is loaded from cache
    all.dec      <- lapply(all.sce, modelGeneVar)
    universe     <- Reduce(intersect, lapply(all.sce, rownames))
    all.sce2     <- lapply(all.sce, "[", i = universe,)
    all.dec2     <- lapply(all.dec, "[", i = universe,)
    normed.sce   <- do.call(multiBatchNorm, all.sce2)
    combined.dec <- do.call(combineVar, all.dec2)
    combined.hvg <- getTopHVGs(combined.dec, n = 5000)

    set.seed(1)
    mnn.sce <- do.call(fastMNN, c(normed.sce,
        list(subset.row = combined.hvg, BSPARAM = RandomParam())))

    set.seed(1)
    mnn.sce <- runUMAP(mnn.sce, dimred = "corrected")
    set.seed(1)
    mnn.sce <- runTSNE(mnn.sce, dimred = "corrected")
  }
  saveRDS(mnn.sce, file = mnn_file)
} else {
  mnn.sce <- readRDS(mnn_file)
}
```

# Testing `k` for stability

`k` in `buildSNNGraph` sets how many neighbors each cell connects to, and it
determines how many communities Louvain clustering finds. 

The sweep clusters ten independent 80% subsamples of the cells at each `k` and
compares pairs of subsamples on the cells they share. Agreement is the adjusted
Rand index, which scores whether two clusterings agree about putting each pair
of cells together or apart, adjusted for the agreement expected by chance.

The sweep takes about 45 minutes on the full object, so it is run separately by
`src/slurm_stable_k.sh`, which reads the merged object and writes to
`results/<date>_stable_k`. The call is shown here for reference.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
# strip to the coordinates: fastMNN output carries a reconstructed assay that
# nothing here reads, and find_stable_k subsets the object once per iteration
lean = SingleCellExperiment(assays = list(), colData = colData(mnn.sce))
reducedDim(lean, "corrected") = reducedDim(mnn.sce, "corrected")
colnames(lean) = colnames(mnn.sce)

stab = find_stable_k(lean,
                     k_range      = c(10, 20, 30, 40, 50),
                     n_iterations = 10,
                     use.dimred   = "corrected",   # not "PCA"; this object has none
                     prop         = 0.8,
                     seed         = 42)

plot_stability_metrics(stab)$data
```

```{r}
stable_k_file = paste0(params$project_dir, "/results/", results_date,
                       "_stable_k/stability_by_k.csv")

if (!file.exists(stable_k_file))
  stop("missing ", stable_k_file,
       ". The stability sweep has not been run. ",
       "Submit src/slurm_stable_k.sh and let it finish first.")

stability_cols = c("k", "mean_n_clusters", "cv_n_clusters", "mean_ari", "min_ari")

stability = read.csv(stable_k_file, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

missing_cols = setdiff(stability_cols, colnames(stability))
if (length(missing_cols) > 0)
  stop(stable_k_file, " is missing column(s): ",
       paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", "),
       ". It should be the stability_by_k.csv written by src/run_stable_k.R.")

stability = stability %>%
  dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(stability_cols)) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(k)

datatable(stability %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~signif(., 4))),
          rownames = FALSE, options = list(dom = "t", ordering = FALSE))
```

```{r, fig.width=9, fig.height=3.5}
p_stab = (ggplot(stability, aes(k, mean_ari)) +
            geom_line(colour = "darkgreen") + geom_point(size = 2) +
            geom_vline(xintercept = snn_k, linetype = "dotted") +
            geom_hline(yintercept = 0.9, linetype = "dashed", colour = "red") +
            # keeps the 0.8-to-1 frame when the data allows it, but widens
            # rather than clipping a k that scored below it
            coord_cartesian(ylim = c(min(0.8, min(stability$mean_ari,
                                                  na.rm = TRUE)), 1)) +
            ylab("mean ARI between subsamples") +
            ggtitle("Stability")) |
          (ggplot(stability, aes(k, mean_n_clusters)) +
            geom_line(colour = "steelblue") + geom_point(size = 2) +
            geom_vline(xintercept = snn_k, linetype = "dotted") +
            ylab("mean number of clusters") +
            ggtitle("Cluster count"))

p_stab
ggsave(p_stab, file = paste0(results_dir, "/clustering_stability.png"),
       width = 9, height = 3.5)
```

```{r}
best_k = stability$k[which.max(stability$mean_ari)]
```

`r paste0("**The most stable k is ", best_k, "**, with a mean ARI of ", signif(max(stability$mean_ari), 3), ". The document clusters at k = ", snn_k, if (best_k == snn_k) ", the most stable value." else ".", " Mean ARI ranges from ", signif(min(stability$mean_ari), 3), " to ", signif(max(stability$mean_ari), 3), " across the sweep.")`

A high ARI at a given `k` means the clusters reproduce when the cells are
perturbed at that `k`. It does not mean the partition is insensitive to `k`
itself. `r paste0("Mean cluster count moves from ", signif(max(stability$mean_n_clusters), 3), " to ", signif(min(stability$mean_n_clusters), 3), " across the sweep.")` The sweep supports "the clustering is reproducible at the
chosen `k`", not "this is the correct number of clusters".

Stability alone does not pick a resolution, because a coarser clustering is
generally more stable. `r if (best_k > min(stability$k) && best_k < max(stability$k)) "Here the most stable value lies inside the sweep rather than at its coarsest end, but that peak is still not the biologically correct resolution." else "Here the most stable value lies at the edge of the sweep, so the sweep may not contain the peak."`

# Cluster

The shared nearest neighbor graph is built on the corrected space at
`k` = `r snn_k`, and communities are found with Louvain.

```{r}
if (build_merged) {
  set.seed(1)
  g <- buildSNNGraph(mnn.sce, use.dimred = "corrected", k = snn_k)
  set.seed(1)
  merged.sce <- mnn.sce
  colLabels(merged.sce) <- factor(igraph::cluster_louvain(g)$membership)
  saveRDS(merged.sce, file = merged_file)
  writeLines(as.character(snn_k), k_stamp)
} else {
  merged.sce <- readRDS(merged_file)
}
```

```{r}
# uncorrected counts on the same cells, for every quantification below
if (build_combined) {
  universe <- Reduce(intersect, lapply(all.sce, rownames))
  all.sce2 <- lapply(all.sce, "[", i = universe,)
  all.sce2 <- lapply(all.sce2, function(x) {
    colData(x)     <- colData(x)[, "sample", drop = FALSE]
    reducedDims(x) <- list()
    rowData(x)     <- rowData(x)[, character(0)]
    x
  })
  combined.sce <- do.call(cbind, all.sce2)
  saveRDS(combined.sce, file = combined_file)
} else {
  combined.sce <- readRDS(combined_file)
}

# the clustering and the counts must describe the same cells in the same order
stopifnot(identical(colnames(combined.sce), colnames(merged.sce)))
```

`r paste0("The atlas holds ", format(ncol(merged.sce), big.mark = ","), " cells in ", nlevels(colData(merged.sce)$label), " clusters.")`

# Per-cluster QC

Genes detected and total counts per cell, broken down by cluster. 

```{r}
# recomputed from the counts rather than carried from the per-sample objects,
# so the numbers describe the shared gene universe that combined.sce holds and
# that every downstream test uses
qc_cell = scuttle::perCellQCMetrics(combined.sce)

cluster_qc = data.frame(
  cluster  = colData(merged.sce)$label,
  detected = qc_cell$detected,
  sum      = qc_cell$sum,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# mitochondrial percentage cannot be recomputed here, since combined.sce does
# not record which genes are mitochondrial. It is taken from the per-sample
# objects, but only if their concatenation lines up with combined.sce exactly.
mito_src = try(do.call(rbind, lapply(all.sce, function(x) {
  cd = as.data.frame(colData(x))
  if (!"subsets_Mito_percent" %in% colnames(cd)) return(NULL)
  data.frame(barcode = colnames(x), mito = cd$subsets_Mito_percent,
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
})), silent = TRUE)

have_mito = !inherits(mito_src, "try-error") && !is.null(mito_src) &&
            identical(mito_src$barcode, colnames(combined.sce))
if (have_mito) cluster_qc$mito_percent = mito_src$mito
```

`r if (have_mito) "" else "**Mitochondrial percentage is not shown.** The per-sample objects either do not carry it or their cell order does not match the combined object, so it is omitted rather than aligned on an assumption."`

```{r}
qc_summary = cluster_qc %>%
  group_by(cluster) %>%
  summarize(n_cells        = dplyr::n(),
            median_genes   = round(median(detected)),
            median_counts  = round(median(sum)),
            median_mito    = if (have_mito) round(median(mito_percent), 2) else NA_real_,
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(median_genes))

if (!have_mito) qc_summary$median_mito = NULL

write.csv(qc_summary, file = paste0(results_dir, "/cluster_qc.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)

datatable(qc_summary, rownames = FALSE,
          options = list(dom = "t", paging = FALSE))
```

# Stage and library metadata

```{r}
library_meta = data.frame(
  batch   = c("UND1_C00004336", "UND2_C00004362", "TF_C00004337", "TM_C00004374"),
  library = c("Undifferentiated.1", "Undifferentiated.2", "Female", "Male"),
  stage   = c("larva", "larva", "transformer", "transformer"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

observed   = sort(unique(as.character(colData(merged.sce)$batch)))
unexpected = setdiff(observed, library_meta$batch)
if (length(unexpected) > 0)
  stop("Library identifier(s) in the object but not in library_meta: ",
       paste(unexpected, collapse = ", "),
       ". Add them rather than silently dropping cells.")

cell_key = data.frame(barcode = colnames(combined.sce),
                      label   = as.character(colData(merged.sce)$label),
                      batch   = as.character(colData(merged.sce)$batch),
                      stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
  left_join(library_meta, by = "batch")

all_clusters = as.character(sort(as.integer(unique(cell_key$label))))

datatable(library_meta, rownames = FALSE, options = list(dom = "t"))
```

**Stage is confounded with collection date and technical batch.** Larvae were
collected in July and transformers in November, so nothing computed from this
dataset can say how much of the larva-to-transformer difference is
developmental. The analysis below asks whether the populations correspond, not
what makes them differ.

# Cluster composition

```{r}
# one function, used here and again after the split, so the two sets of tables
# are built the same way and any difference between them is a real one
composition_of = function(lab_vec, lab_levels) {
  data.frame(label   = factor(as.character(lab_vec), levels = lab_levels),
             library = cell_key$library,
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
    dplyr::count(label, library, name = "n") %>%
    tidyr::complete(label, library = library_meta$library,
                    fill = list(n = 0)) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(id_cols = label, names_from = library,
                       values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
    mutate(larva       = Undifferentiated.1 + Undifferentiated.2,
           transformer = Female + Male,
           Total       = larva + transformer) %>%
    arrange(label)
}

add_percents = function(tbl) {
  tbl %>%
    mutate(across(c(Undifferentiated.1, Undifferentiated.2, Female, Male,
                    larva, transformer),
                  ~round(100 * .x / Total, 1),
                  .names = "pct_{.col}"))
}

comp_bar = function(tbl, title) {
  tbl %>%
    dplyr::select(label, all_of(library_meta$library)) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_longer(-label, names_to = "library", values_to = "n") %>%
    mutate(library = factor(library, levels = library_meta$library)) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = n, y = label, fill = library)) +
    geom_col(position = "fill") +
    scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
    xlab("proportion of cells") + ylab("cluster") + ggtitle(title)
}

stage_bar = function(tbl, title) {
  tbl %>%
    dplyr::select(label, larva, transformer) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_longer(-label, names_to = "stage", values_to = "n") %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = n, y = label, fill = stage)) +
    geom_col(position = "fill") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(larva = "#009292", transformer = "#9e2f7f")) +
    xlab("proportion of cells") + ylab("cluster") + ggtitle(title)
}

flag_one_library = function(tbl, threshold = 90) {
  add_percents(tbl) %>%
    rowwise() %>%
    mutate(max_lib_pct = max(c_across(c(pct_Undifferentiated.1,
                                        pct_Undifferentiated.2,
                                        pct_Female, pct_Male)))) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    filter(max_lib_pct >= threshold) %>%
    dplyr::select(label, Total, max_lib_pct)
}
```

# Cluster correspondence across stages

Each cluster's markers are computed from larval cells alone and, separately,
from transformer cells alone, on uncorrected values. If the genes that define
cluster 8 among larvae are the genes that define cluster 8 among transformers,
and they match cluster 8 better than any other cluster, then cluster 8 is the
same population on both sides.

**No corrected values enter this test**, so its answer does not depend on the
`fastMNN` correction. The test compares marker lists within each stage rather
than expression levels across stages, so a uniform shift between collections
does not change the result.

**Every result is read against a replicate reference computed the same way.**
Undifferentiated.1 against Undifferentiated.2 is two animals of the same stage
collected on the same date. It shows how well clusters correspond when only
replicate variation separates the sides. That sets the ceiling, and the ceiling
is below 100%.

## Clusters with at least 20 enough cells from each side to compare

```{r}
min_cells_side = 20

side_counts = cell_key %>%
  dplyr::count(label, library, name = "n") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(id_cols = label, names_from = library,
                     values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  mutate(larva       = Undifferentiated.1 + Undifferentiated.2,
         transformer = Female + Male) %>%
  arrange(as.integer(label))

write.csv(side_counts, file = paste0(results_dir, "/cells_per_cluster_per_side.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)

# paging = FALSE because dom = "t" hides the pagination control without
# disabling pagination, so a table longer than ten rows silently loses the rest
datatable(side_counts, rownames = FALSE,
          options = list(dom = "t", paging = FALSE))
```

```{r}
core_clusters = side_counts %>%
  filter(Undifferentiated.1 >= min_cells_side,
         Undifferentiated.2 >= min_cells_side,
         transformer        >= min_cells_side) %>%
  pull(label)

# One cell depth per cluster, shared by the replicate and stage comparisons, so the
# floor is measured on the same number of cells as the test it calibrates.
# Subsampling each comparison to its own minimum would put them on different
# cell counts and the margins would not be comparable.
core_n = side_counts %>%
  filter(label %in% core_clusters) %>%
  transmute(label, n = pmin(Undifferentiated.1, Undifferentiated.2, transformer))
core_n = setNames(core_n$n, core_n$label)
```

`r paste0(length(core_clusters), " of ", nrow(side_counts), " clusters have at least ", min_cells_side, " cells in Undifferentiated.1, in Undifferentiated.2 and in the transformers, so both comparisons run on that set.")`

## Correspondence

### Procedure

Two comparisons are run, each splitting the cells into two sides:

* **replicate**, Undifferentiated.1 against Undifferentiated.2
* **stage**, the two larval libraries pooled against the two transformer
  libraries pooled

Both run on the same cluster set at the same per-cluster cell depth, so their results
are directly comparable and the replicate one serves as the reference for the
other.

For each comparison:

1. **Set a cell depth for every cluster.** This is
   `min(n in UND1, n in UND2, n in transformers)` for that cluster. The larval
   pool is UND1 plus UND2 so it can never be the smallest and is left out of the
   minimum.

2. **Repeat the following 10 times.**

    a. From side A, draw that many cells of every eligible cluster, without
       replacement. Do the same from side B, so both sides contribute the same
       number of cells for every cluster.

    b. Run `findMarkers` separately on each side's drawn cells, with the eligible
       clusters as the grouping and **the same cluster set as the competing
       background on both sides**. Settings are `test.type = "t"`,
       `direction = "up"`, `pval.type = "some"`, and `lfc` set, so the ranking
       reflects effect size rather than cell number. 

    c. For each cluster on each side, **keep only genes below the FDR cutoff**,
       order them by FDR then by p-value, and take the top `n_top` of those. The
       order is imposed explicitly rather than taken from whatever order
       `findMarkers` returns. The filter matters because `findMarkers` ranks
       every gene rather than returning only the significant ones, so an
       unfiltered top `n_top` would pad a weakly marked cluster's list with
       whatever ranked next. A list is therefore as long as the cluster has
       evidence for, up to `n_top`, and can be empty.

    d. Build a square matrix over the eligible clusters. Entry `[i, j]` is the
       percentage overlap between side A's list for cluster `i` and side B's list
       for cluster `j`, using the **shorter of the two lists as the denominator**:
       `100 * length(intersect(A_i, B_j)) / min(length(A_i), length(B_j))`. The
       denominator is not always `n_top`, because a cluster with few significant
       genes returns a shorter list.

3. **Average the 10 matrices elementwise.** Everything below is read off the
   averaged matrix, not off any single draw.

4. **For each cluster `i`, read four numbers off that matrix.**

    * `self_similarity` is the diagonal, `M[i, i]`: how far cluster `i`'s list on
      one side agrees with its own list on the other.
    * `best_forward` is the column of the largest value in row `i`: the cluster on
      side B that side A's cluster `i` most resembles.
    * `best_reverse` is the row of the largest value in column `i`: the cluster on
      side A that side B's cluster `i` most resembles.
    * `margin` is `M[i, i]` minus the largest off-diagonal value in row `i`: how
      far the self-match beats its strongest competitor. Negative means some other
      cluster matched better than the cluster matched itself.

5. **A cluster corresponds when it is its own best match in both directions**,
   that is `best_forward == i` and `best_reverse == i`. This is stricter than a
   positive margin, since a diffuse cluster can be several clusters' best partner
   without any of them choosing it back.

6. **Classify each cluster** using the replicate result as the control:
   a cluster whose replicate comparison is not reciprocal is **untestable at this
   cell depth**, since it cannot find itself even between two animals of the same
   stage; otherwise it **corresponds** or **fails** according to its stage result.

### Limits of equal cell depth

Step 2a gives both sides the same number of cells, so neither side is favored by
sample size. It does not make the two sides equally informative. When one side
is scarce:

* **Draws repeat.** A side drawn from a pool barely larger than the draw returns
  nearly the same cells every time, so averaging over the 10 draws reduces its
  noise very little. A side drawn from thousands averages over ten different
  subsets.
* **Lists shorten.** Fewer cells yield fewer significant genes, so that side's
  list is shorter and the denominator in step 2d shrinks with it. On a list of
  ten, one chance overlap moves the score by ten points, so a self-match can
  lose to a competitor on noise alone. The `sig_larva` and `sig_transformer`
  columns report the list lengths.
* **Boundaries follow the larger side.** Where a cluster holds almost all of one
  side's cells, the draw takes the whole population, including cells at its
  boundary, while the other side contributes a random sample of a
  well-populated core. The cluster boundary came from a clustering of all
  cells, so it mostly reflects the larger side.

A scarce side can therefore fail without the two populations differing. The
untestable category exists for this reason, and failures are reported with
their cell counts.

```{r}
n_top      = 50
fdr_cut    = 0.01
n_draws    = 10

# Significant genes only, then the top n of those.
#
# findMarkers ranks every gene rather than returning only the significant ones,
# so taking the top n without filtering would hand a cluster with eight real
# markers a list of n padded with whatever ranked next. Only the significant
# part can be expected to recur on the other side, so the padding measures the
# stability of a weak tail. Filtering first means a list is as long as the
# cluster has evidence for, and never longer.
top_markers_for = function(marker_list, lab, n = n_top, fdr = fdr_cut) {
  if (is.null(marker_list) || !lab %in% names(marker_list)) return(character(0))
  df = marker_list[[lab]]
  if (nrow(df) == 0) return(character(0))
  # sorted explicitly rather than trusting the order findMarkers returns
  ord = if (all(c("FDR", "p.value") %in% colnames(df))) order(df$FDR, df$p.value)
        else if ("FDR" %in% colnames(df)) order(df$FDR) else seq_len(nrow(df))
  keep = ord[which(df$FDR[ord] < fdr)]
  rownames(df)[keep][seq_len(min(n, length(keep)))]
}

# Per-gene effect size: the mean across every pairwise comparison.
# summary.logFC is not used, because under pval.type = "some" it comes from
# whichever pairwise comparison supplied the summary p-value, which varies per
# gene and per run.
marker_effect = function(df) {
  lf = grep("^logFC\\.", colnames(df), value = TRUE)
  if (length(lf) == 0) return(rep(NA_real_, nrow(df)))
  v = rowMeans(as.matrix(as.data.frame(df[, lf, drop = FALSE])), na.rm = TRUE)
  names(v) = rownames(df)
  v
}

# lfc is set because with thousands of cells a log-fold change of 0.02 clears
# FDR 0.01, and an unthresholded ranking measures sample size rather than effect
markers_for_cells = function(cells, clusters_keep) {
  lab = factor(cell_key$label[cells], levels = clusters_keep)
  findMarkers(combined.sce[, cells], lab, test.type = "t",
              direction = "up", lfc = lfc_thresh, pval.type = "some")
}

similarity_matrix = function(mA, mB, clusters) {
  tA = lapply(clusters, function(cl) top_markers_for(mA, cl)); names(tA) = clusters
  tB = lapply(clusters, function(cl) top_markers_for(mB, cl)); names(tB) = clusters
  sim = matrix(NA_real_, length(clusters), length(clusters),
               dimnames = list(clusters, clusters))
  for (i in clusters) for (j in clusters) {
    d = min(length(tA[[i]]), length(tB[[j]]))
    sim[i, j] = if (d == 0) NA_real_ else
      100 * length(intersect(tA[[i]], tB[[j]])) / d
  }
  # lists are now significant genes only, so their length is the number of
  # markers the cluster actually has at this cell depth, capped at n_top. It is both
  # the diagnostic and the denominator above, and a cluster with none gives an
  # empty list, which scores NA rather than zero.
  list(sim   = sim,
       sig_A = lengths(tA),
       sig_B = lengths(tB))
}

run_comparison = function(sideA_libs, sideB_libs, clusters_keep, n_by_cluster,
                          seed = 1) {
  inA = which(cell_key$library %in% sideA_libs)
  inB = which(cell_key$library %in% sideB_libs)

  stopifnot(all(clusters_keep %in% names(n_by_cluster)))
  n_by_cluster = n_by_cluster[clusters_keep]

  avail = sapply(clusters_keep, function(cl)
    min(sum(cell_key$label[inA] == cl), sum(cell_key$label[inB] == cl)))
  if (any(avail < n_by_cluster))
    stop("requested cell depth exceeds available cells for cluster(s): ",
         paste(clusters_keep[avail < n_by_cluster], collapse = ", "))

  set.seed(seed)
  acc = NULL; acc_sigA = NULL; acc_sigB = NULL
  for (d in seq_len(n_draws)) {
    draw_side = function(idx) {
      unlist(lapply(clusters_keep, function(cl) {
        pool = idx[cell_key$label[idx] == cl]
        # sampled by position: sample(x, n) with x of length 1 draws from
        # seq_len(x) instead of from x
        pool[sample(length(pool), n_by_cluster[[cl]])]
      }))
    }
    out = similarity_matrix(markers_for_cells(draw_side(inA), clusters_keep),
                            markers_for_cells(draw_side(inB), clusters_keep),
                            clusters_keep)
    acc      = if (is.null(acc))      out$sim   else acc      + out$sim
    acc_sigA = if (is.null(acc_sigA)) out$sig_A else acc_sigA + out$sig_A
    acc_sigB = if (is.null(acc_sigB)) out$sig_B else acc_sigB + out$sig_B
  }
  list(sim   = acc      / n_draws,
       sig_A = acc_sigA / n_draws,
       sig_B = acc_sigB / n_draws,
       n_by_cluster = n_by_cluster)
}
```

Cell numbers are matched per cluster across every side of every comparison.
Library is not blocked, because library is the variable being measured.
Similarity matrices from ten independent draws are averaged before any verdict
is read.

```{r}
# The depth scheme is part of the cache key, not just the tuning parameters, so
# results computed under a different scheme are not silently reused.
depth_tag = paste0("commonN", sum(core_n))

comparison_file = paste0(Robject_out_dir, "/stage_correspondence_", depth_tag,
                         "_", n_top, "_lfc", lfc_thresh, "_", n_draws, "draws.Rds")

if (file.exists(comparison_file)) {
  comparisons = readRDS(comparison_file)
} else {
  comparisons = list(
    replicate = run_comparison("Undifferentiated.1", "Undifferentiated.2",
                               core_clusters, core_n),
    stage     = run_comparison(c("Undifferentiated.1", "Undifferentiated.2"),
                               c("Female", "Male"), core_clusters, core_n))
  saveRDS(comparisons, file = comparison_file)
}
```

A cluster **corresponds** when it is its own best match in both directions. The
**margin** is how far the self-match sits above the strongest competitor.

```{r}
reciprocal_from_sim = function(sim) {
  cls = rownames(sim)
  do.call(rbind, lapply(cls, function(i) {
    row = sim[i, ]; col = sim[, i]; off = row[names(row) != i]
    fwd = names(which.max(row)); rev = names(which.max(col))
    best_off = if (all(is.na(off))) NA_real_ else max(off, na.rm = TRUE)
    data.frame(cluster = i, self_similarity = sim[i, i],
               best_forward = if (length(fwd)) fwd else NA_character_,
               best_reverse = if (length(rev)) rev else NA_character_,
               reciprocal   = identical(fwd, i) && identical(rev, i),
               margin       = sim[i, i] - best_off,
               stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }))
}

recip = bind_rows(lapply(names(comparisons), function(nm)
  reciprocal_from_sim(comparisons[[nm]]$sim) %>%
    mutate(comparison = nm,
           n_per_side = comparisons[[nm]]$n_by_cluster[cluster],
           # mean over draws of each side's marker list length: the number of
           # significant genes, capped at n_top
           sig_A      = round(comparisons[[nm]]$sig_A[cluster], 1),
           sig_B      = round(comparisons[[nm]]$sig_B[cluster], 1)))) %>%
  dplyr::select(comparison, cluster, n_per_side, sig_A, sig_B,
                self_similarity, best_forward, best_reverse, reciprocal, margin)

write.csv(recip, file = paste0(results_dir, "/SuppTable_reciprocal_matches.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)

datatable(recip %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(., 1))),
          filter = "top", rownames = FALSE)
```

## Replicate control

A cluster that does not correspond to itself **between the two larval animals**,
at the cell depth its stage test uses, is not resolvable at that depth. Its
stage result carries no information and is not counted as a failure.

```{r}
stage_tbl = recip %>% filter(comparison == "stage") %>%
  dplyr::select(cluster, n_per_side,
                sig_larva = sig_A, sig_transformer = sig_B,
                self_stage = self_similarity,
                margin_stage = margin, reciprocal_stage = reciprocal,
                best_forward, best_reverse)

rep_tbl = recip %>% filter(comparison == "replicate") %>%
  dplyr::select(cluster, self_rep = self_similarity,
                margin_rep = margin, reciprocal_rep = reciprocal)

outcome_tbl = stage_tbl %>%
  left_join(rep_tbl, by = "cluster") %>%
  left_join(side_counts %>% dplyr::select(cluster = label, larva, transformer),
            by = "cluster") %>%
  mutate(outcome = dplyr::case_when(
           !reciprocal_rep  ~ "untestable at this cell depth",
           reciprocal_stage ~ "corresponds across stages",
           TRUE             ~ "fails across stages"),
         # which side's marker list broke the match
         direction = dplyr::case_when(
           reciprocal_stage                                  ~ "both directions agree",
           best_forward == cluster & best_reverse != cluster ~ "transformer side fails",
           best_forward != cluster & best_reverse == cluster ~ "larval side fails",
           best_forward == best_reverse                      ~ "both point to the same other cluster",
           TRUE                                              ~ "both fail, and disagree")) %>%
  dplyr::select(cluster, larva, transformer, n_per_side,
                sig_larva, sig_transformer,
                self_rep, margin_rep, reciprocal_rep,
                self_stage, margin_stage, reciprocal_stage,
                best_forward, best_reverse, direction, outcome) %>%
  arrange(match(outcome, c("fails across stages", "corresponds across stages",
                           "untestable at this cell depth")),
          as.integer(cluster))

write.csv(outcome_tbl, file = paste0(results_dir, "/SuppTable_stage_outcomes.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)

datatable(outcome_tbl %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(., 1))),
          filter = "top", rownames = FALSE)
```

```{r}
short_cut  = 0.6 * n_top
short_side = outcome_tbl %>%
  filter(outcome == "fails across stages",
         pmin(sig_larva, sig_transformer) < short_cut) %>%
  dplyr::select(cluster, larva, transformer, n_per_side,
                sig_larva, sig_transformer, margin_stage)
```

**`sig_larva` and `sig_transformer` are the lengths of each side's marker list**,
averaged over the draws and capped at `r n_top`.

The lists hold significant genes only, so a list is as long as the cluster's
evidence. That length is also the denominator in step 2d, so a cluster with few
markers is scored on a small number: on a list of ten, a single chance overlap
is worth ten points. Read a high similarity on a short list with that in mind,
and read a failure on a short list as underpowered.

A cluster with no significant genes on one side scores `NA` rather than zero. In
the replicate comparison that makes the cluster untestable. In the stage
comparison it counts as a failure, and the list lengths show why.

`r if (nrow(short_side) == 0) paste0("Every failing cluster has at least ", round(short_cut), " significant genes on both sides, so no failure rests on a short list.") else paste0("**", nrow(short_side), " of the failing clusters have fewer than ", round(short_cut), " significant genes on one side: ", paste(short_side$cluster, collapse = ", "), ".** Read their results as underpowered, and compare each list length with the cell count in the same row.")`

```{r}
n_corresponds = sum(outcome_tbl$outcome == "corresponds across stages")
n_fails       = sum(outcome_tbl$outcome == "fails across stages")
n_untestable  = sum(outcome_tbl$outcome == "untestable at this cell depth")
n_readable    = n_corresponds + n_fails

rep_recip = sum(recip$reciprocal[recip$comparison == "replicate"])
rep_n     = sum(recip$comparison == "replicate")

fails_tbl = outcome_tbl %>% filter(outcome == "fails across stages")
```

`r paste0("**", rep_recip, " of ", rep_n, " clusters correspond between the two larval animals**, at the same cell depths the stage test runs at. Across the stage boundary, ", n_corresponds, " of ", n_readable, " readable clusters correspond and ", n_fails, " do not.")`

`r if (n_untestable == 0) "Every cluster is resolvable at its own cell depth, so no stage result is discarded for lack of cells." else paste0(n_untestable, " cluster(s) are untestable at this cell depth: ", paste(outcome_tbl$cluster[outcome_tbl$outcome == "untestable at this cell depth"], collapse = ", "), ". These fail to find themselves even between the two larval animals, so their stage result reflects cell numbers rather than stage. They are reported and not counted either way.")`

Read the `direction` column before deciding what a failure means:

* **One side fails.** The cluster is usually short of cells on the failing side.
* **Both fail and disagree.** The two sides point at different partners. This is
  the strongest failure.
* **Both point to the same other cluster.** This is the only case that indicates
  merging with that cluster.

```{r, fig.width=13, fig.height=5}
  as.data.frame(as.table(comparisons[[nm]]$sim)) %>%
    setNames(c("side_A", "side_B", "similarity")) %>%
    mutate(comparison = nm))) %>%
  mutate(side_A = factor(side_A, levels = all_clusters),
```

# Splitting

A cluster is split into a larval and a transformer half when it fails in both
directions and has enough cells on each side to describe. Everything downstream
runs on that labeling.

Other failures are left whole. A cluster that fails in one direction only, or
has too few cells on a side, would yield a half too small to characterize, and
its failure is better explained by scarcity.

```{r}
split_min_cells  = 300   # per side, enough to compute a marker profile
split_min_margin = 20    # replicate margin, so the cluster is well separated

split_candidates = outcome_tbl %>%
  filter(outcome == "fails across stages",
         direction == "both fail, and disagree",
         margin_rep >= split_min_margin,
         larva >= split_min_cells, transformer >= split_min_cells) %>%
  pull(cluster)

datatable(outcome_tbl %>%
            filter(outcome == "fails across stages") %>%
            dplyr::select(cluster, larva, transformer, margin_rep, direction) %>%
            mutate(splits = cluster %in% split_candidates),
          rownames = FALSE, options = list(dom = "t", paging = FALSE))
```

**The split halves differ by stage, collection date, technical batch, animal and, where one side is a single transformer library, by sex as well.** The split records that the two halves are not one population by marker evidence. It does not say what makes them different.

```{r}
# Each split cluster becomes two labels; every other cluster keeps its own, so
# the marker computation later runs over one factor covering all cells and the
# split halves compete against the same background as everything else.
final_label = cell_key$label
for (cl in split_candidates) {
  hit = cell_key$label == cl
  final_label[hit] = paste0(cl, "_", cell_key$stage[hit])
}

# unsplit clusters first in their original order, then the split halves, so the
# ordering is stable rather than alphabetical
final_label = factor(final_label,
                     levels = c(setdiff(all_clusters, split_candidates),
                                sort(unique(final_label[grepl("_", final_label)]))))

cell_key$final_label = as.character(final_label)

stopifnot(!any(is.na(final_label)),
          length(final_label) == nrow(cell_key))

# Cell type names supplied by the Chung-Davidson lab for this labeling. Their
# 12L and 12T are the larval and transformer halves of the split cluster. The
# row order is the order of the Figure 1 legend.
anno = tibble::tribble(
  ~final_label,      ~cell_type,
  "1",               "Fibroblasts",
  "2",               "Mesonephric cells",
  "3",               "Migrating erythrocytes",
  "4",               "Granulosa cells",
  "5",               "PGCs/oogonia/oocytes",
  "6",               "Endothelial cells",
  "7",               "Podocytes",
  "8",               "Erythrocytes",
  "9",               "Migrating pre-granulosa cells",
  "10",              "Hemopoietic stem cells",
  "11",              "Migrating leukocytes",
  "12_transformer",  "Bipotential gonadal supporting cells",
  "12_larva",        "Mitotic macrophages",
  "13",              "Macrophages",
  "14",              "Migrating/mitotic pre-granulosa cells",
  "15",              "Mitotic spermatogonia",
  "16",              "Spermatocytes I",
  "17",              "Spermatocytes II",
  "18",              "Migrating spermatocytes")

# These names describe this clustering at this k and this doublet rate. Louvain
# renumbers on any rerun, so a mismatch here means the names no longer apply and
# must be re-derived rather than reused.
missing_anno = setdiff(levels(final_label), anno$final_label)
extra_anno   = setdiff(anno$final_label, levels(final_label))
if (length(missing_anno) > 0 || length(extra_anno) > 0)
  stop("The annotation does not match this labeling. ",
       if (length(missing_anno)) paste0("Unnamed label(s): ",
           paste(missing_anno, collapse = ", "), ". ") else "",
       if (length(extra_anno)) paste0("Named but absent: ",
           paste(extra_anno, collapse = ", "), ". ") else "",
       "Re-derive the annotation for this clustering before relabeling.")

cell_key = cell_key %>% left_join(anno, by = "final_label")

# The per-cell assignment, saved. Everything else this document writes is
# aggregated by label, so without this the split labeling exists only for the
# duration of the knit and nothing downstream can use it.
cell_labels = cell_key %>%
  dplyr::select(barcode, batch, library, stage,
                cluster = label, final_label, cell_type)

write.csv(cell_labels,
          file = paste0(results_dir, "/cell_cluster_labels.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)

# also as an Rds, so a downstream document can attach it to an SCE by name
# without a read.csv and a match()
saveRDS(setNames(cell_labels$final_label, cell_labels$barcode),
        file = paste0(Robject_out_dir, "/final_label.Rds"))

datatable(as.data.frame(table(final_label = final_label)) %>%
            dplyr::rename(n_cells = Freq) %>%
            dplyr::select(final_label, n_cells),
          rownames = FALSE, options = list(dom = "t", paging = FALSE))
```

The cell type names are held back until after the marker sections, so the
evidence is read before the interpretation. They are applied in **Cell type
annotation** below.

`r if (length(split_candidates) == 0) "No cluster met the conditions, so the final labeling is the original clustering unchanged." else paste0("Cluster(s) ", paste(split_candidates, collapse = ", "), " were split, giving ", nlevels(final_label), " labels from ", length(all_clusters), " clusters.")`

The per-cell assignment is written to `cell_cluster_labels.csv`, one row per
barcode with its library, stage, original cluster and final label, and as
`Robjects/final_label.Rds`, a named vector for attaching to an object directly:

```r
labs <- readRDS("<results_dir>/Robjects/final_label.Rds")
sce$final_label <- labs[colnames(sce)]
```

Note that `merged.sce` is saved before the split, so its own `label` column is
the original clustering. Anything wanting the split labeling has to take it
from one of these two files rather than from the object.

# Cluster marker genes

Markers for every cluster of the final labeling, computed on uncorrected
counts with library blocked. 

**No effect size threshold is applied to the test.** `findMarkers` is run without
`lfc`, so the null is that the log fold change is zero and the saved result is
complete. Effect size is applied afterwards, as a filter on `meanLogFC`, where a
working list is needed.

```{r}
# no lfc in the call, so the cached object is not interchangeable with one
# written by an earlier lfc-thresholded version. The filename says so.
marker_file_rds = paste0(Robject_out_dir, "/final_markers_nolfc.Rds")

if (file.exists(marker_file_rds)) {
  final_markers = readRDS(marker_file_rds)
} else {
  final_markers = findMarkers(combined.sce, final_label, test.type = "t",
                              block = cell_key$library, direction = "up",
                              pval.type = "some")
  saveRDS(final_markers, file = marker_file_rds)
}

gene_description = read.csv(paste0(object_dir, "/gene_descritption.csv"),
                            stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
```

```{r}
# both counts, because FDR alone is not a useful cutoff at this cell number:
# with tens of thousands of cells a log fold change of 0.02 clears FDR 0.01 and
# the count measures sample size rather than biology
marker_counts = purrr::map_dfr(names(final_markers), function(lab) {
  d = final_markers[[lab]]
  eff = marker_effect(d)
  data.frame(cluster        = lab,
             n_FDR          = sum(d$FDR < 0.01),
             n_FDR_and_lfc  = sum(d$FDR < 0.01 & eff >= lfc_thresh),
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
})

datatable(marker_counts, rownames = FALSE,
          options = list(dom = "t", paging = FALSE))
```

`r paste0("FDR alone gives a median of ", format(round(median(marker_counts$n_FDR)), big.mark = ","), " genes per cluster, and requiring a mean log fold change of at least ", lfc_thresh, " leaves a median of ", format(round(median(marker_counts$n_FDR_and_lfc)), big.mark = ","), ".")`

`r if (all(marker_counts$n_FDR_and_lfc > 0)) "Every cluster has at least one marker passing both." else paste0("**Cluster(s) ", paste(marker_counts$cluster[marker_counts$n_FDR_and_lfc == 0], collapse = ", "), " have no gene passing both FDR < 0.01 and a mean log fold change of ", lfc_thresh, ".** At this effect size such a cluster cannot be distinguished from the rest of the atlas, and it is absent from the overlap and ontology results below. For a split half this argues against the split. Its genes remain in the unfiltered file, so the cutoff can be relaxed.")` 

```{r}
# built once without a cutoff; the filtered table is derived from it, so the two
# cannot drift apart
markers_unfiltered = purrr::map_dfr(names(final_markers), function(lab) {
  df  = final_markers[[lab]]
  ord = order(df$FDR, df$p.value)
  data.frame(cluster   = lab,
             Gene      = rownames(df)[ord],
             p.value   = df$p.value[ord],
             FDR       = df$FDR[ord],
             meanLogFC = marker_effect(df)[ord],
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}) %>%
  left_join(gene_description, by = "Gene")

unfiltered_file = paste0(results_dir, "/cluster_marker_genes_unfiltered.csv")
write.csv(markers_unfiltered, file = unfiltered_file, row.names = FALSE)

# the working list: significant and of a usable size. Both cutoffs are applied
# here rather than in the test, so the unfiltered table above stays complete.
markers_all = markers_unfiltered %>%
  filter(FDR < 0.01, meanLogFC >= lfc_thresh) %>%
  # ordered by effect within a cluster, since FDR alone ranks by cell number
  group_by(cluster) %>%
  arrange(desc(meanLogFC), FDR, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  ungroup()

write.csv(markers_all, file = paste0(results_dir, "/cluster_marker_genes.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
```

`r paste0("**cluster_marker_genes_unfiltered.csv** holds ", format(nrow(markers_unfiltered), big.mark = ","), " rows, every one of ", format(dplyr::n_distinct(markers_unfiltered$Gene), big.mark = ","), " genes against each of ", dplyr::n_distinct(markers_unfiltered$cluster), " clusters, at ", round(file.size(unfiltered_file) / 1e6), " MB. **cluster_marker_genes.csv** is the same table filtered to FDR < 0.01 and mean log fold change at least ", lfc_thresh, ", ", format(nrow(markers_all), big.mark = ","), " rows. Everything below runs on the filtered list.")`

The unfiltered file carries `p.value`, `FDR` and `meanLogFC` for every gene
against every cluster, so a gene missing from the working list can be looked up
rather than assumed untested. The `.Rds` in `Robjects/` holds the full
per-comparison `logFC.*` columns if an individual pairwise contrast is needed;
`meanLogFC` is their mean, used because `summary.logFC` under
`pval.type = "some"` comes from whichever comparison supplied the summary
p-value and so is not a fixed contrast.

```{r}
datatable(markers_all %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~signif(., 3))),
          filter = "top", rownames = FALSE)
```

# Comparison with the curated markers

Rows are marker sets, columns are clusters, color is the significance of the
overlap with each cluster's full marker list, every gene passing FDR < 0.01 and
a mean log fold change of at least `r lfc_thresh`.

The lists are of unequal length, because clusters differ in how many genes
distinguish them. The hypergeometric accounts for list size, so this does not
bias the p-values. It does affect power: a cluster with a long list can reach
significance on a weaker proportional overlap than one with a short list. Read a
strong overlap in a cluster with few markers as the stronger result of the two.

```{r}
curated = read.csv(paste0(data_dir, "/", marker_file),
                   stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(loc_id = trimws(loc_id)) %>%
  filter(loc_id %in% rownames(combined.sce))

# Exactly two columns. phyperOverlapSets renames the first two positionally and
# ignores anything else, so an extra column would not error; it would change
# what distinct() collapses. A gene carrying two labels would then appear twice,
# inflating the set size that goes into the hypergeometric.
known_markers = curated %>%
  dplyr::select(Gene = loc_id, CellType = CellTypeMarkerSet) %>%
  distinct()

# the display label for each gene, kept separate for the reason above. The S1
# symbol is used rather than the gene table's, so figures carry the name the
# collaborators' sheet uses.
marker_symbols = curated %>%
  dplyr::select(Gene = loc_id, WangGeneID = symbol) %>%
  distinct()

stopifnot(!any(duplicated(marker_symbols$Gene)))

# the full lfc-filtered list, not a fixed top n. Feeds both the overlap heatmap
# below and the GO enrichment in the next section, so the two run on the same
# gene set rather than on different definitions of "this cluster's markers".
marker_test_genes = markers_all %>%
  dplyr::select(Gene, cluster) %>%
  mutate(cluster = paste0("cluster", cluster)) %>%
  distinct()

list_sizes = marker_test_genes %>% dplyr::count(cluster, name = "n_markers")

set_sizes = curated %>% dplyr::count(CellTypeMarkerSet, name = "n_genes") %>%
  mutate(below_coherence_floor = n_genes < 3)

datatable(set_sizes, rownames = FALSE,
          options = list(dom = "t", paging = FALSE))
```

`r paste0(nrow(known_markers), " gene-to-set assignments resolve against this count matrix, over ", dplyr::n_distinct(known_markers$CellType), " sets. ", sum(set_sizes$below_coherence_floor), " set(s) hold fewer than three genes. In those rows a single significant overlap is one gene.")`

`r paste0("Cluster marker lists run from ", format(min(list_sizes$n_markers), big.mark = ","), " to ", format(max(list_sizes$n_markers), big.mark = ","), " genes (median ", format(round(median(list_sizes$n_markers)), big.mark = ","), "), across ", nrow(list_sizes), " clusters.")`

```{r, fig.width=9}
plot_marker_overlap_heatmap(
  known_markers    = known_markers,
  test_genes       = marker_test_genes,
  background_n     = nrow(combined.sce),
  gene_description = gene_description,
  overlaps_file    = paste0(results_dir, "/cluster_marker_gene_overlaps.csv"),
  pvals_file       = paste0(results_dir, "/cluster_marker_overlap_pvalues.csv"),
  plot_file        = paste0(results_dir, "/cluster_marker_overlap_heatmap.png"))
```

```{r}
gaf_file      = file.path(genome_dir,
                          "GCF_010993605.1_kPetMar1.pri_gene_ontology.gaf")
```

```{r}
gaf = read.delim(gaf_file, header = FALSE, comment = "!") %>%
  filter(!grepl("NOT", V4)) %>%
  dplyr::select(V3, V5) %>%
  dplyr::rename(GOID = "V5", Gene = "V3") %>%
  distinct()

# terms too small are noise, terms too large are uninformative
keep_go = gaf %>% group_by(GOID) %>% tally() %>%
  filter(n > 10, n < 200) %>% pull(GOID)
gaf = gaf %>% filter(GOID %in% keep_go)

go_names = read.delim(go_names_file, header = FALSE)
colnames(go_names) = c("GOID", "GOName")

go_scores = run_go_enrichment(
  gaf              = gaf,

  go_names         = go_names,
  test_genes       = marker_test_genes,

  overlaps_file    = paste0(results_dir, "/cluster_GO_overlaps.csv"),
  pvals_file       = paste0(results_dir, "/cluster_GO_overlap_pvalues.csv"),
  pval_filter      = 0.01)

datatable(go_scores %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~signif(., 3))),
          filter = "top", rownames = FALSE)
```

# Marker expression across all clusters

Every curated marker against every cluster, on uncorrected, depth-normalized
values. Dot size is the percentage of cells in the cluster expressing the gene,
and color is the mean log expression.

This differs from the overlap heatmap, which tests whether a cell type's markers
are *enriched* among a cluster's data-derived markers. A gene can be enriched in
a cluster relative to the others while barely transcribed there.

```{r}
marker_ids = intersect(unique(known_markers$Gene),
                       rownames(combined.sce))

bubble_mat = as.matrix(logcounts(combined.sce)[marker_ids, , drop = FALSE])

# labels come from cell_key, which is where final_label lives; merged.sce was
# never given that column. And they are iterated as characters over the factor
# levels rather than coerced to integer, because a split label such as
# "12_larva" becomes NA under as.integer and would be dropped silently.
bubble_lab = cell_key$final_label
stopifnot(length(bubble_lab) == ncol(bubble_mat))

marker_bubble = purrr::map_dfr(levels(final_label), function(k) {
  sub = bubble_mat[, bubble_lab == k, drop = FALSE]
  data.frame(cluster        = k,
             Gene           = marker_ids,
             n_cells        = ncol(sub),
             pct_expressing = 100 * rowMeans(sub > 0),
             mean_logexpr   = rowMeans(sub),
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}) %>%
  left_join(known_markers, by = "Gene",
            relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
  left_join(marker_symbols, by = "Gene") %>%
  mutate(CellType = factor(CellType),
         cluster  = factor(cluster, levels = levels(final_label)))

stopifnot(!any(is.na(marker_bubble$WangGeneID)))

stopifnot(setequal(levels(droplevels(marker_bubble$cluster)), levels(final_label)))

write.csv(marker_bubble,
          file = paste0(results_dir, "/canonical_marker_expression_per_cluster.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r, fig.width=11, fig.height=13}
p_bubble = ggplot(marker_bubble,
                  aes(x = cluster, y = WangGeneID,
                      size = pct_expressing, colour = mean_logexpr)) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_colour_viridis_c() +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(0.4, 5)) +
  facet_grid(CellType ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  theme(strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, size = 6),
        axis.text.y  = element_text(size = 6),
        axis.text.x  = element_text(size = 8, angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        panel.grid.major = element_line(linewidth = .2)) +
  xlab("cluster") + ylab(NULL) +
  labs(size = "% expressing", colour = "mean logexpr")

p_bubble
ggsave(p_bubble, file = paste0(results_dir, "/canonical_marker_bubble_all_clusters.png"),
       width = 11, height = 13)
```

The underlying values are written to
`canonical_marker_expression_per_cluster.csv`, one row per gene per cluster with
the percentage expressing and the mean log expression.

# Dissociation response

Enzymatic dissociation at 37 degrees induces the AP-1 and immediate-early genes.
Expression of them reports how the tissue was handled rather than what the cell
was doing in the animal, so a cluster carrying them is a candidate for being an
artifact of the protocol. The genes are listed in `r ieg_marker_file`.

This is a description, not a correction. Some immediate-early expression is
expected everywhere, and the question is whether any cluster carries much more
than the rest.

```{r}
ieg_path = paste0(data_dir, "/", ieg_marker_file)
stopifnot(file.exists(ieg_path))

ieg_genes = read.csv(ieg_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(loc_id = trimws(loc_id)) %>%
  filter(loc_id %in% rownames(combined.sce)) %>%
  dplyr::select(Gene = loc_id, WangGeneID = symbol) %>%
  distinct()

ieg_tab = NULL
ieg_h   = max(4, round(0.22 * nrow(ieg_genes) + 2))
if (nrow(ieg_genes) > 0) {
  ieg_mat = as.matrix(logcounts(combined.sce)[ieg_genes$Gene, , drop = FALSE])
  ieg_lab = cell_key$final_label
  stopifnot(length(ieg_lab) == ncol(ieg_mat))

  ieg_bubble = purrr::map_dfr(levels(final_label), function(k) {
    sub = ieg_mat[, ieg_lab == k, drop = FALSE]
    data.frame(cluster        = k,
               Gene           = ieg_genes$Gene,
               n_cells        = ncol(sub),
               pct_expressing = 100 * rowMeans(sub > 0),
               mean_logexpr   = rowMeans(sub),
               stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }) %>%
    left_join(ieg_genes, by = "Gene") %>%
    mutate(cluster = factor(cluster, levels = levels(final_label)))

  write.csv(ieg_bubble,
            file = paste0(results_dir, "/dissociation_response_per_cluster.csv"),
            row.names = FALSE)

  # the set as one number per cluster, so clusters can be ranked against
  # each other rather than read gene by gene
  ieg_tab = ieg_bubble %>%
    group_by(cluster) %>%
    summarise(n_cells      = dplyr::first(n_cells),
              n_genes      = dplyr::n(),
              mean_logexpr = signif(mean(mean_logexpr), 3),
              pct_detected = round(mean(pct_expressing), 1),
              .groups = "drop") %>%
    arrange(desc(mean_logexpr))

  write.csv(ieg_tab,
            file = paste0(results_dir, "/dissociation_response_by_cluster.csv"),
            row.names = FALSE)

  datatable(ieg_tab, rownames = FALSE, options = list(pageLength = 20))
}
```

`r if (is.null(ieg_tab)) "None of the immediate-early genes is in the data." else { top = ieg_tab[1, ]; nxt = ieg_tab[2, ]; paste0(nrow(ieg_genes), " of the immediate-early genes are in the data. The highest scoring cluster is ", top$cluster, " at ", top$mean_logexpr, " mean log expression, detected in ", top$pct_detected, " percent of its cells on average, against ", nxt$mean_logexpr, " for ", nxt$cluster, ". A cluster well clear of the rest here is one to look at before it is given a cell type.") }`

```{r, fig.width=10, fig.height=if (exists("ieg_h")) ieg_h else 6}
if (!is.null(ieg_tab)) {
  p_ieg = ggplot(ieg_bubble,
                 aes(x = cluster, y = WangGeneID,
                     size = pct_expressing, colour = mean_logexpr)) +
    geom_point() +
    scale_colour_viridis_c() +
    scale_size_continuous(range = c(0.4, 5)) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 9) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, size = "% of cells", colour = "mean log expression",
         title = "Immediate-early gene expression by cluster")

  print(p_ieg)
  ggsave(p_ieg, file = paste0(results_dir, "/dissociation_response.png"),
         width = 10, height = ieg_h, dpi = 300)
}
```

# Summary

```{r}
n_clusters = nlevels(colData(merged.sce)$label)
n_core     = nrow(outcome_tbl)   # clusters that entered the comparison at all

# Every subset row carries its own denominator, because there are three of them:
# all clusters, the core set that had enough cells per side to be compared, and
# the readable set whose replicate comparison succeeded. Each level is a subset
# of the one above, and the rows are ordered so that nesting is visible.
stopifnot(n_untestable + n_readable == n_core, n_core <= n_clusters)

summary_tbl = data.frame(
  stage = c("atlas", "atlas",
            "entering the test", "entering the test",
            "of those compared", "of those compared",
            "control", "stage test", "stage test",
            "outcome", "outcome"),
  quantity = c("cells",
               "clusters before splitting",
               paste0("too few cells to compare (under ", min_cells_side,
                      " on a side)"),
               "compared",
               "untestable at their own cell depth",
               "readable across the stage boundary",
               "correspond between the two larval animals",
               "correspond across the stage boundary",
               "fail across the stage boundary",
               "clusters split",
               "labels in the final labeling"),
  value = c(format(ncol(merged.sce), big.mark = ","),
            as.character(n_clusters),
            paste0(n_clusters - n_core, " of ", n_clusters),
            paste0(n_core, " of ", n_clusters),
            paste0(n_untestable, " of ", n_core),
            paste0(n_readable, " of ", n_core),
            paste0(rep_recip, " of ", rep_n),
            paste0(n_corresponds, " of ", n_readable),
            paste0(n_fails, " of ", n_readable),
            if (length(split_candidates) == 0) "0"
              else paste0(length(split_candidates), " (",
                          paste(split_candidates, collapse = ", "), ")"),
            as.character(nlevels(final_label))),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

datatable(summary_tbl, rownames = FALSE, colnames = c("", "", ""),
          options = list(dom = "t", ordering = FALSE, paging = FALSE))
```

```{r, fig.width=12, fig.height=5, dev = "png", dpi = 600}
# merged.sce above, so the embedding attaches by position
fig1_tsne = reducedDim(merged.sce, "TSNE")
fig1_cells = cell_key %>%
  dplyr::mutate(TSNE1         = fig1_tsne[, 1],
                TSNE2         = fig1_tsne[, 2],
                CellType      = factor(unname(fig1_types[final_label]),
                                       levels = unname(fig1_types)),
                cluster_label = unname(fig1_short[final_label]))

p_fig1_tsne = plot_tsne(df           = fig1_cells,
                        color_col    = "CellType",
                        label_col    = "cluster_label",
                        palette      = fig1_palette,
                        color_levels = unname(fig1_types),
                        point_size   = 0.5,
                        text_color   = "black",
                        bg_color     = "white",
                        text_size    = 2) +
  theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = "black", color = NA),
        legend.key       = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA))

# the library colors used in 02, so a library is the same color in every figure
lib_cols = c("Female"             = "#FF6DB6",
             "Male"               = "#006ddb",
             "Undifferentiated.1" = "#009292",
             "Undifferentiated.2" = "#b66ddf")

fig1_comp = comp_post %>%
  dplyr::mutate(label = as.character(label)) %>%
  dplyr::select(label, dplyr::all_of(names(lib_cols))) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-label, names_to = "library", values_to = "n") %>%
  dplyr::group_by(label) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(frac = n / sum(n)) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  # cluster 1 at the top, in the order of the tSNE legend
  dplyr::mutate(cluster = factor(unname(fig1_short[label]),
                                 levels = rev(unname(fig1_short))),
                library = factor(library, levels = names(lib_cols)))

stopifnot(setequal(unique(fig1_comp$label), anno$final_label))

p_fig1_comp = ggplot(fig1_comp, aes(x = frac, y = cluster, fill = library)) +
  geom_col(width = .85) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = lib_cols) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), labels = scales::percent) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 8) +
  theme(axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
        axis.line.y  = element_blank()) +
  labs(x = "cells in the cluster", y = NULL, fill = "library")

p_fig1 = (p_fig1_tsne | p_fig1_comp) +
  patchwork::plot_layout(widths = c(2.2, 1)) +
  patchwork::plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A") &
  theme(plot.tag = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"))

p_fig1
ggsave(p_fig1, file = paste0(results_dir, "/Fig1_tsne.png"),
       width = 12, height = 5, dpi = 600)
```

`r paste0("**Figure 1. Clusters of all cells and their library composition.** **(A)** tSNE of the ", format(ncol(merged.sce), big.mark = ","), " cells from four libraries: two undifferentiated larvae and one female and one male transformer. The tSNE is computed on the fastMNN-corrected space of the four libraries. Cells are colored by cell type, and each number marks the median position of its cluster's cells. The legend gives the number of cells of each type. Clusters are Louvain communities of a shared nearest neighbor graph (k = ", snn_k, ") built on the corrected space. Cluster 12 is split into a transformer half (12T) and a larval half (12L). Its larval and transformer cells did not match each other by marker gene overlap in either direction. **(B)** The percentage of each cluster's cells from each library.")`

# Everything written by this document

Built by listing the results directory and looking each file up, rather than by
keeping a list by hand. A file with no description, or a description with no
file, is reported below instead of passing unnoticed.

```{r}
file_notes = c(
  "median_stats.csv"              = "Per library after doublet removal: cells, median counts, median genes detected and median percent mitochondrial.",
  "clustering_stability.png"      = "Mean ARI between subsamples and mean cluster count across k, with the chosen k marked.",
  "all_cells_tsne.png"            = "tSNE of all cells colored by cluster before splitting.",
  "tsne_by_library.png"           = "Each library over the full embedding.",
  "cluster_qc.csv"                = "Per cluster before splitting: cells, median genes detected, median counts and median percent mitochondrial.",
  "cluster_qc_genes.png"          = "Genes detected per cell by cluster.",
  "cluster_qc_counts.png"         = "Counts per cell by cluster.",
  "cluster_qc_mito.png"           = "Percent mitochondrial per cell by cluster.",
  "cluster_composition.csv"       = "Cells per cluster from each library and stage, as counts and percentages, before splitting.",
  "cluster_composition_by_library.png" = "Library composition of each cluster before splitting.",
  "cluster_composition_by_stage.png"   = "Stage composition of each cluster before splitting.",
  "cells_per_cluster_per_side.csv" = "Cells per cluster on the larval and transformer sides, which decides whether a cluster can be compared.",
  "SuppTable_reciprocal_matches.csv" = "Every cluster in both comparisons, replicate and stage: list lengths, self similarity, best match each way, reciprocity and margin.",
  "SuppTable_stage_outcomes.csv"  = "One row per compared cluster: the replicate control, the stage test, which side broke the match, and the outcome.",
  "cross_boundary_similarity.png" = "Marker list overlap between every pair of clusters, for the replicate and the stage comparison.",
  "self_match_margin.png"         = "Each cluster's margin over its strongest competitor, replicate against stage.",
  "cell_cluster_labels.csv"       = "One row per cell: barcode, library, stage, original cluster, final label and cell type.",
  "cluster_composition_after_split.csv" = "Cells per final label from each library and stage, as counts and percentages.",
  "cluster_composition_by_library_after_split.png" = "Library composition of each final label.",
  "cluster_composition_by_stage_after_split.png"   = "Stage composition of each final label.",
  "cluster_marker_genes_unfiltered.csv" = "Every gene for every final label: p-value, FDR and mean log fold change, with gene descriptions.",
  "cluster_marker_genes.csv"      = "The working marker list: FDR < 0.01 and mean log fold change of at least lfc_thresh.",
  "cluster_marker_gene_overlaps.csv"   = "Which genes each cluster's markers share with each curated marker set.",
  "cluster_marker_overlap_pvalues.csv" = "Hypergeometric test of each cluster's markers against each curated marker set.",
  "cluster_marker_overlap_heatmap.png" = "Those tests as a heatmap.",
  "cluster_GO_overlaps.csv"       = "Which marker genes carry each enriched GO term, per cluster.",
  "cluster_GO_overlap_pvalues.csv" = "GO enrichment of each cluster's marker genes.",
  "canonical_marker_expression_per_cluster.csv" = "Percent expressing and mean log expression of every curated marker in every final label.",
  "canonical_marker_bubble_all_clusters.png"    = "Those values as a bubble plot, faceted by marker set.",
  "dissociation_response_per_cluster.csv" = "The immediate-early genes per final label, gene by gene.",
  "dissociation_response_by_cluster.csv"  = "The immediate-early set as one score per final label.",
  "dissociation_response.png"     = "Immediate-early gene expression by final label.",
  "cell_type_annotation.csv"      = "Each final label with its cell type name and cell count.",
  "Fig1_tsne.png"                 = "Figure 1: tSNE by cell type and the library composition of each cluster.")

in_dir  = sort(setdiff(list.files(results_dir), "Robjects"))

# The table describes what this document writes. The results directory also
# holds whatever earlier runs left behind, and those are named below rather
# than given rows with no description.
on_disk = intersect(names(file_notes), in_dir)
unknown = setdiff(in_dir, names(file_notes))
missing = setdiff(names(file_notes), in_dir)

file_size = function(f)
  format(structure(file.size(f), class = "object_size"), units = "auto")

export_tab = data.frame(
  file = on_disk,
  size = sapply(file.path(results_dir, on_disk), file_size),
  what = unname(file_notes[on_disk]),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

datatable(export_tab, rownames = FALSE, escape = FALSE,
          options = list(pageLength = 40, dom = "tp",
                         columnDefs = list(list(width = "240px", targets = 0))))
```

`r if (length(unknown) > 0) paste0(length(unknown), " file(s) in the directory are not written by this document and are left out of the table: ", paste(unknown, collapse = ", "), ". Either an earlier version wrote them, or they are new and need a line in file_notes.") else ""`

`r if (length(missing) > 0) paste0("Described but not written on this run: ", paste(missing, collapse = ", "), ".") else ""`

`r paste0("Written to ", results_dir, ".")`

## Objects read by later documents

These are written to the shared `_no_doublets` directory, or to `Robjects`, and
are reused rather than rebuilt when they already exist. The modification time
says which run wrote each one.

```{r}
object_notes = c(
  "doublet_removal_stats.csv" = "Cells before and after doublet removal per library.",
  "doublet_rate_used.txt"     = "The doublet rate the per-library objects were built at.",
  "all.sce.Rds"               = "The per-library objects after doublet removal, normalized, with PCA.",
  "mnn.sce.Rds"               = "The fastMNN merge of the four libraries, with tSNE.",
  "merged.sce.Rds"            = "The merge with its clustering at snn_k.",
  "clustering_k_used.txt"     = "The k the cached clustering was built at.",
  "combined.sce.Rds"          = "Uncorrected counts on the same cells, for every quantification.")

object_tab = data.frame(
  file = c(names(object_notes), "Robjects/final_label.Rds"),
  path = c(file.path(object_dir, names(object_notes)),
           file.path(Robject_out_dir, "final_label.Rds")),
  what = c(unname(object_notes),
           "The final label of every cell, named by barcode."),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
  dplyr::filter(file.exists(path)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(size     = sapply(path, file_size),
                modified = format(file.mtime(path), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")) %>%
  dplyr::select(file, size, modified, what)

datatable(object_tab, rownames = FALSE,
          options = list(dom = "t", paging = FALSE, ordering = FALSE))
```

`r paste0("The shared objects are in ", object_dir, ".")`
